articles.headline: High schooler arrested after stolen gun found in backpack
articles.excerpt: A 16-year-old at Millington Central Middle High School was arrested after school officers found a stolen handgun in his backpack. A photo of a student holding the gun as school let out led officers to the teen, now charged with theft and weapon possession.

articles.headline: Back to School: McAlester debuts restricted backpack policy
articles.excerpt: McAlester Public Schools opened the year with a new restricted backpack policy for grades 5-12, part of a wave of Oklahoma districts tightening what students can carry onto campus in a bid to keep weapons out of classrooms and protect staff and students.

articles.headline: 1 arrested, 4 detained after student reportedly photographed with gun at Fort Worth high school, authorities say
articles.image_alt: Police outside O.D. Wyatt High School
articles.excerpt: A social media photo appearing to show students with a gun inside O.D. Wyatt High School forced a full lockdown on the first day of classes in Fort Worth. An 18-year-old was arrested and four others detained; no weapon was found on campus.

articles.headline: Franklin County student arrested, accused of issuing threats against school, peers
articles.excerpt: A student in the Sesser-Valier school district was arrested after allegedly making verbal threats against school staff and fellow students. Franklin County deputies were notified Aug. 9 and say there is no ongoing threat to school personnel or students.

articles.headline: Teen kills classmates, teachers, and his grandparents in Thai gun rampage, police say
articles.excerpt: A teenage gunman killed five teachers and staff members, fellow students and his grandparents in a rampage at Debsirin Nonthaburi School near Bangkok before taking his own life. The attack left more than 20 injured at the 3,000-student campus.

articles.headline: Ponchatoula student accused of threatening school shooting on first day of classes
articles.excerpt: A Ponchatoula teenager was booked on one count of terrorizing after a Crimestoppers tip flagged a videoed threat to commit a shooting at Ponchatoula High School. Louisiana deputies made the arrest before students returned for the first day of classes.

articles.headline: Before Teacher Shield is needed, provide resources to prevent aggression
articles.excerpt: Louisiana's Teacher Shield Act took effect Aug. 1, requiring students who assault school employees to be placed in alternative schools for at least two semesters. A former educator argues the new law must be paired with prevention resources and behavioral supports.

articles.headline: FCPS addresses impacts of Senate Bill 101 on teacher safety
articles.excerpt: Fayette County Public Schools officials outlined how Kentucky's Senate Bill 101 will reshape discipline, requiring expulsion of students who intentionally injure educators. The new protections take effect as teachers return for the school year.

articles.headline: 75% of Educators Expect Student Behavior to Be a Challenge This Year. What Else?
articles.excerpt: An EdWeek Research Center survey of more than 1,000 teachers and administrators found 75% rank student behavior as a major challenge heading into 2026-27 — ahead of engagement and staffing — underscoring the strain educators carry into the new year.

articles.headline: What to know about San Antonio schools' clear backpack policies
articles.excerpt: Harlandale ISD becomes the latest San Antonio district to require clear or mesh backpacks for all students in 2026-27, a first for the 11,500-student district as area schools layer on security measures aimed at keeping weapons off campus.

archive.headline: St. Johns teens charged with cache of homemade guns and explosives
archive.excerpt: St. Johns County deputies say two middle schoolers amassed makeshift firearms and explosive material alongside white supremacist writings and a manifesto referencing mass shooters. An anonymous FortifyFL tip led to arrests; the elder teen will be tried as an adult.

archive.headline: Students caught with weapons at Augusta schools on first day of class
archive.excerpt: On the first days of the new school year, a firearm was found in a student's backpack at Richmond Hill Elementary and a knife was detected at Westside High's metal detectors. Officials credited layered security measures and urged parents to check backpacks daily.

archive.headline: Former student accused of school shooting threat transferred to ADC over parole violation
archive.excerpt: A 21-year-old former Greenbrier student accused of threatening a mass shooting at East Side Elementary was transferred to the Arkansas Department of Corrections on a parole violation. She remains in custody, charged with threatening mass violence on school property.

archive.headline: Lee County Schools roll out new safety measures for 2026-27 year
archive.excerpt: Every Lee County Schools staff member began the year wearing a panic-button badge that can summon help instantly or trigger a full campus lockdown. A newly created executive director of school safety role makes protecting students and staff a dedicated focus.

archive.headline: School districts strengthen security while weapons possession offenses drop to 20-year low
archive.excerpt: Weapons possession offenses in North Carolina public schools fell to their lowest level since statewide records began in 2006-07, state data show, even as districts continue adding detection systems and security staff ahead of the new school year.

archive.headline: Georgia teen arrested for making threat days into new school year
archive.excerpt: A 14-year-old Morgan County Middle School student was taken into custody and charged with terroristic threats just two days into the new school year. The sheriff said threats of school violence are 'not negotiable' and each will be fully investigated.

archive.headline: Houston ISD Police Department readies safety, security measures for 2026-27 school year
archive.excerpt: Houston ISD police announced expanded safety measures ahead of the Aug. 10 start of the 2026-27 school year, adding more than 100 guards to monitor campuses along with around-the-clock patrols, officials said at an Aug. 4 news conference.

archive.headline: Apalachee shooter's father Colin Gray processed into Georgia prison
archive.excerpt: Colin Gray, the first parent in the U.S. convicted of murder for a school shooting carried out by his child, has been processed into Georgia's maximum-security Jackson prison to begin a 15-year sentence for the Apalachee attack that killed two teachers and two students.

archive.headline: Metter juvenile charged after threat against high school faculty, staff and students
archive.excerpt: Metter police charged a juvenile with criminal attempt to commit murder and terroristic threats after a threatened act of violence against faculty, staff and students at Metter High School, days before classes resumed in Candler County.

archive.headline: Two Middle Georgia schools receive anonymous threats ahead of first days of school
archive.image_alt: Law enforcement search at Georgia school
archive.excerpt: Wheeler County and Telfair County school districts were swept by law enforcement with K-9 teams after anonymous robocall threats arrived just ahead of the first days of school. The GBI is investigating the source of the calls.

archive.headline: Judge to sentence Colin Gray after closing arguments in Apalachee school shooting case
archive.image_alt: Colin Gray in courtroom during trial
archive.excerpt: Colin Gray, the first parent of a school shooter convicted of murder, faces up to 180 years for giving his son the rifle used at Apalachee High School. Prosecutors asked for 80 years as the sentencing hearing opened Thursday.

archive.headline: Teen gets life without parole for killing 4 at Georgia's Apalachee High School
archive.excerpt: Colt Gray was sentenced to life in prison without parole for the 2024 Apalachee High School shooting that killed teachers Richard Aspinwall and Cristina Irimie and two students. The judge said the attack was carried out “for the infamy of it.”

archive.headline: US School Violence Fast Facts
archive.excerpt: CNN's updated fast facts compile the nationwide toll of school violence, tracking shootings and attacks on campuses — a running record of the incidents that have made educator safety a national concern heading into the 2026-27 school year.

archive.headline: Dorchester District Two adding armed security force ahead of new school year
archive.excerpt: Dorchester District Two will deploy 14 armed, SLED-trained school security officers across its high schools and alternative school this fall, adding to the district's 37 school resource officers as campuses harden ahead of the new year.

archive.headline: Lamar County Schools introducing weapons detectors, AI camera detection
archive.image_alt: Weapons detection scanners at school entrance
archive.excerpt: Lamar County Schools will make weapons detection a daily practice at every middle and high school campus this year, pairing walk-through detectors with AI camera monitoring as districts across Mississippi harden campuses before classes resume.

archive.headline: Colt Gray, Georgia school shooter, pleads guilty and victims deliver emotional statements in court
archive.image_alt: Courtroom scene at Apalachee plea hearing
archive.excerpt: Colt Gray pleaded guilty to all 55 counts in the 2024 Apalachee High School shooting that killed teachers Richard Aspinwall and Cristina Irimie and two students. Families and wounded survivors urged the judge to deny any possibility of parole.

archive.headline: Metro Atlanta school districts increase safety measures ahead of upcoming school year
archive.image_alt: Weapons detection system at school entrance
archive.excerpt: Atlanta Public Schools has added tactical and drone units to its police force, while Gwinnett County, Georgia's largest district, now runs AI weapons detectors at every middle and high school, part of a metro-wide push to harden campuses before students return.

archive.headline: Dorchester County agencies hold active shooter drill ahead of new school year
archive.image_alt: First responders during school safety drill
archive.excerpt: With the new school year weeks away, first responders and school officials in Dorchester County ran worst-case active shooter scenarios at Williams Memorial Elementary, drilling the coordination needed to protect educators and students in a real attack.

archive.headline: Teacher Sues Howard Co. Board Of Education: Report
archive.excerpt: A math specialist at Bonnie Branch Middle School is suing the Howard County Board of Education for $750,000, alleging it failed to protect her after a parent blocked her in a conference room in 2023 — an encounter she says later triggered a stroke.

archive.headline: First Responders to Meet for Annual School Safety Planning
archive.excerpt: Law enforcement, fire, EMS, emergency dispatchers, school resource officers and school administrators will gather ahead of the new school year to review and strengthen safety procedures across local campuses.

archive.headline: AFT Re-elects Officers, Hears from Union and Political Leaders, Passes Suite of Resolutions at 2026 Convention
archive.excerpt: At its 2026 convention, the AFT adopted a resolution declaring violence is never 'part of the job,' demanding enforceable workplace violence protections for teachers and school staff — noting 1 in 4 nonfatal workplace violence incidents target school employees.

archive.headline: Opelousas woman accused of terrorizing, assault on teacher
archive.image_alt: St. Landry Parish Sheriff's Office insignia
archive.excerpt: A 25-year-old Opelousas woman was arrested after allegedly threatening a school paraprofessional and the St. Landry Parish Sheriff's Office. She faces a felony terrorizing count and four felony counts of assault on a school teacher.

archive.headline: Ascension Public Schools rolling out upgrades ahead of new school year
archive.excerpt: The Louisiana district is investing $2.5 million in AI-powered weapons detection systems at every campus and requiring clear backpacks and water bottles for all students as part of a broader push for faster, safer school entry.

archive.headline: Public schools across Kentucky will see changes starting Wednesday
archive.image_alt: School bus outside a Kentucky school
archive.excerpt: Kentucky's Senate Bill 101 takes effect July 15, requiring districts to expel students in grades 6-12 for at least a year if they injure or attempt to injure school staff. The law answers teacher unions' calls to put educator safety first, mandating law enforcement reporting of assaults.

archive.headline: Detroit man charged in fatal shooting of custodian outside Chrysler Elementary School
archive.image_alt: Police photo related to school shooting case
archive.excerpt: Prosecutors charged Kevin Flagg, 43, with second-degree murder in the July 2 shooting of Devin Burns, a 25-year-old contracted custodian for Detroit Public Schools, killed in the Chrysler Elementary parking lot after a dispute escalated. Flagg returns to court July 20.

archive.headline: School shootings in the US: Fast facts
archive.excerpt: CNN's updated tracker counts at least 31 school shootings in the U.S. so far in 2026 — 21 on K-12 grounds — leaving at least 22 people dead and 23 injured, underscoring the threat educators and staff face on campus.

archive.headline: Henry County schools invest in teachers, safety ahead of new school year
archive.excerpt: Henry County's school board approved budget updates directing new money to higher employee pay and additional school security ahead of the 2026-27 year — a district-level bet that safer campuses help retain educators.

archive.headline: Gov. Green signs key measures to strengthen Hawaiʻi's education system
archive.excerpt: Hawaiʻi's HB 1888 makes harassment of school employees a misdemeanor, requires threats be reported to police within 48 hours, and lets the attorney general help educators obtain restraining orders against aggressors.

archive.headline: Student busted with gun at Manhattan high school: NYPD
archive.excerpt: A 17-year-old was arrested after an unannounced scanning at West Side High School turned up a loaded, defaced 9mm pistol in his bag. He faces three counts of criminal possession of a weapon; no one was injured.
